cases.reasoning: The question asks for Adam's beta_1, beta_2 and epsilon defaults. Page 2 states verbatim: 'Good default settings for the tested machine learning problems are alpha = 0.001, beta1 = 0.9, beta2 = 0.999 and epsilon = 10^-8.' All three requested values (beta_1 = 0.9, beta_2 = 0.999, epsilon = 10^-8) are supplied on the inspected page, so the passage answers the exact question. Proposed 'relevant' is correct.

The supplied page-2 passage gives the default hyperparameters and shows bias-corrected moment estimates (mt/(1-beta_1^t), vt/(1-beta_2^t)) in Algorithm 1, but it does not explain WHY zero initialization of the moment vectors causes a bias toward zero. That explanation is deferred: page 2 only says 'Section 3 explains our initialization bias correction technique'. Judged strictly on the supplied passage (no outside evidence), it answers the 'what are the defaults' part but not the 'why does zero initialization cause bias' part, so 'partially_relevant' is correct.
